technology_decision: Use the CPython native buffer-protocol copy behind Python parent orchestration: it copies into owned bytes under the existing process lock, avoids per-byte boxed list allocation, and materially improves the measured maximum-frame copy without a new FFI or runtime dependency.
scope: P1.3 parent decoder admission and shared-buffer snapshot only. Decoder backend/acquisition, clock mapping, inference and full process-isolation technology review remain open.

research.assessment: Buffer views expose contiguous storage without a per-byte Python list; tobytes creates the required owned snapshot. Selected and exercised on the real RawArray ABI.

Credible native acquisition alternative with configurable queue bounds and C/binding interfaces. Replacing the producer does not remove the parent metadata and ownership boundary; backend comparison remains open, not rejected because of toolchain availability.

Alternative FFmpeg frame/plane binding exposes buffer size and line stride. A migration needs explicit packed-RGB/stride and timing parity; not assumed equivalent or disqualified by installation status.
